summary: Ends the FYI (For Your Information) sub-series of RFCs, which RFC 1150 created for the IETF User Services Area, a body that no longer exists. The IESG does not plan to add more FYI documents. It also obsoletes RFC 1150 and moves it to Historic.

plainLanguage.summary: The FYI sub-series was created for a part of the IETF that no longer met. This RFC records that no new documents will receive FYI numbers and that the existing numbers remain usable in citations.

subtitle: The IESG closes the FYI RFC sub-series and moves RFC 1150 to Historic.

tldr.problem: The FYI RFC sub-series had been created for an IETF User Services Area that no longer met, leaving its original procedures no longer valid.
tldr.mechanism: The IESG records that it will add no more FYI numbers, retains existing FYI numbers for citation, and obsoletes RFC 1150.
tldr.outcome: The FYI sub-series is closed to new additions, and RFC 1150 is moved to Historic.

today: RFC 6360 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1150, moving it to Historic. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6360.

sections.title: The FYI Sub-Series
sections.content:
RFC 1150 established the For Your Information (FYI) sub-series in 1990 for the IETF User Services Area. It was intended as a collection of information about the Internet that could interest a broad audience.

The User Services Area had not met since IETF 53 in March 2001. A total of 38 FYI numbers had been assigned; many other Informational RFCs were not part of the sub-series.
sections.plainLanguage: The FYI series collected Informational RFCs for a broad audience. The group for which it was created had stopped meeting.

sections.title: No New FYI Numbers
sections.content:
The IESG does not intend to add further documents to the FYI sub-series. It will continue producing Informational RFCs, but new Informational RFCs will not receive FYI numbers.

Existing FYI numbers remain attached to their documents and may still be used in citations. A future RFC that obsoletes an existing FYI document will not receive an FYI number.
sections.plainLanguage: No new RFCs will receive an FYI number. Documents that already have one keep it, and the number can still be cited.

sections.title: RFC 1150 Becomes Historic
sections.content:
RFC 6360 obsoletes RFC 1150 and moves it to Historic because its procedural information is no longer valid.

If it becomes desirable to add to the FYI sub-series in the future, new procedures can be developed. The memo anticipates no Internet security issues from these actions.
sections.plainLanguage: The old procedures for assigning FYI numbers are no longer valid. Any future series would need new procedures.

references.text: Malkin, G. and J. Reynolds, "FYI on FYI: Introduction to the FYI Notes", FYI 1, RFC 1150, March 1990.
